newsitem.title: INDIA: Death toll climbs to 234 in India cyclone.
newsitem.headline: Death toll climbs to 234 in India cyclone.

text.p: The death toll from a cyclone that struck India's major crop-growing state of Andhra Pradesh has climbed to 234, relief workers said on Thursday.

"The death toll has gone to 234, and it may climb further," H.S. Brahma, the top state official coordinating relief operations, told Reuters. District officials said the toll was expected to rise rapidly.

The storm, with winds of between 100 and 120 kmh (62 mph to 75 mph), struck India's southeast coast on Wednesday evening, flattening homes, destroying crops and cutting transport and communication links.
Authorities in Hyderabad, the state's capital, said most of the deaths were due to flooding, house collapses and electrocutions.

Communications were disrupted after the cyclone wreaked havoc in the rich rice-growing Godavari river delta, officials said. In East Godavari, where 100,000 homes were destroyed or damaged, at least 169 people have died.
"The toll may be very high, and it may even touch 1,000," Chief Minister V. Chandrababu Naidu told reporters soon after he finished surveying the flooded areas by helicopter.
The cyclone crossed the coast 50 km (30 miles) south of the port of Kakinada.
Power supplies were disrupted and traffic came to a standstill for several hours on the national highway after trees were uprooted.
Authorities said 42 people died in East Godavari district when their boat capsized in the Godavari river.
"These deaths could have been averted if people had heeded the advice of the authorities against venturing out during the cyclone," senior state official M.S. Rajajee told reporters.
But the storm seems to be petering out.
"The system (depression) is weakening," C.V.V. Bhadram, director of the Meteorological Centre, said.
He said it had moved deeper inland and was located close to the town of Khammam in the Telangana region of Andhra Pradesh. The storm was likely to move in a west-north-west direction.
"It will bring rain and strong winds to the area," a meteorological official said.
Local government officials have been alerted to deal with the impact of the storm. The government has asked the military to help with relief operations.
The district administration is providing foodgrains and drinking water to all those who lost their homes.
Officials are still unable to estimate the full extent of the damage to crops.
Last month, floods damaged 1.13 million hectares (3.1 million acres) of land, about eight per cent of farmed areas in Andhra Pradesh.
